transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I suppose what finally made me come in is that my appetite has just been all over the place for months now. There are these stretches where I'll just skip dinner entirely, and I've been losing weight without even trying to. And then other nights, I just... I end up picking at crackers or having a bowl of cereal, mostly because the thought of actually cooking a meal for myself just feels completely pointless right now.
Over these past months when your appetite has been changing and you've been losing weight, how has your mood been? Have you been feeling sad, empty, or depressed?

I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed feeling sad or depressed, exactly. I mean... I guess I just haven't been paying much attention to my mood itself. I haven't really thought about it in those specific terms, so I don't know if I'd say I feel empty. I just know my appetite is off.
Over these past months, have there been activities or things you normally enjoy doing that just don't interest you anymore or don't feel enjoyable?

Well, yes, I suppose so. I mean, I still go through the motions of things I used to love doing. Like, I'll still go out and water the garden, or I'll show up to my book club meetings. But... most of the time it just feels really flat. There's no joy in it anymore. I usually end up leaving the meetings early, or with the garden, sometimes I just look at it and don't even start. It just feels like too much effort for something I don't really care about right now.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days or longer where you felt unusually energetic, very happy or excited, or needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never had a time where I felt unusually energetic or excited, and my sleep hasn't changed in that way either. I just... I haven't had any periods like what you're describing.

Have you ever experienced a period in the past, before these past few months, where you felt depressed, lost interest in things you normally enjoyed, or had significant changes in your appetite or sleep?

No, I don't think so. I can't recall ever feeling like this before... where things just feel so flat and I don't care about my garden or my book club. And my appetite has always been pretty steady until recently. So, no, nothing like this in the past.

You mentioned these changes have been happening for several months now. Are you currently still experiencing this flat mood, loss of interest, and appetite changes right now, or have these symptoms gotten better recently?
Yes, I'm still experiencing all of that right now. It hasn't really gotten any better recently. I'm still just dealing with that same flat feeling and the lack of appetite pretty much every day.
When did these symptoms first start? Can you remember approximately when a few months ago that was?
Actually, it's been quite a bit longer than a few months. Um... this has really been going on since my divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago now.

Since your divorce was finalized about 19 months ago, has there been any period of time—even a few weeks or a couple of months—where you felt better, your mood improved, and you regained interest in things like your garden or book club before it all became flat again?

No, not really. It's just been a steady... flatness since then. I haven't had any breaks where I felt like my old self or wanted to get back into the garden. It's just been the same way the whole time.

In the 19 months since your divorce was finalized, has there been any stretch of time—say, 2 months or more in a row—where you felt back to normal, with your mood and interest in things returning to how they were before all this started?
No, I haven't. Like I was just saying, there hasn't been any break in it. It's just been the same the whole time. I haven't had any months where I felt back to normal.
Just to be clear: before your divorce was finalized 19 months ago, you were feeling okay—you had your normal mood, you enjoyed your garden and book club, and your appetite was normal?

Yes, exactly. Um... before that, everything was fine. I was just my normal self. I still enjoyed getting out in the garden and going to the book club, and my appetite was fine. It really just all shifted after the divorce was finalized.
